title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-Prem Reference, Packaging, Day-2 Ops, Upgrade & Rollback, Customer Requirements
author: Samira Kaur
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended practices, reference architectures, packaging guidance, day-2 operational procedures, upgrade and rollback playbooks, and a customer requirements library for Private Deployments (VPC and on-prem). It is intended for platform engineers, SREs, and customer engineering teams executing or supporting private deployments.

Scope

- VPC-based private deployments (cloud-hosted customer VPC peering, Transit Gateway, private-link variants)
- Air-gapped and on-prem packaged deployments (customer-owned data center, private cloud)
- Day-2 operations: monitoring, backups, scaling, incident response
- Upgrade/rollback procedures for control plane and data plane components
- Customer requirements: networking, IAM, compliance, and acceptance tests

Audience and Ownership

- Primary audience: eng-private-deployments, eng-infra, eng-sre, customer success engineering
- Document owner: eng-private-deployments (contact: @samira.kaur)
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any major runtime or packaging change

High-level Reference Architectures

1) VPC-hosted Private Deployment (recommended for cloud customers)

- Control plane components (operators, management API) run in Redwood-managed control subnet or in a dedicated management account when required.
- Data plane (inference nodes) deployed in customer's VPC or in a dedicated VPC owned by the customer with private connectivity to Redwood control plane via PrivateLink or IPsec VPN.
- Suggested network zones: management, inference, storage, observability.
- Minimum inbound/outbound rules: allow egress to Redwood control plane endpoints on port 443; open NFS/S3 endpoints internally for model artifact sync; restrict access to metrics and tracing endpoints to observability CIDR blocks.

2) On-prem / Air-Gapped Deployment (recommended for regulated workloads)

- All runtime components packaged as validated container images + signed artifact bundles.
- Deployment via customer-provided Kubernetes (1.24-1.27 supported) or a validated VM-based bundle for air-gapped infra.
- Optional appliance packaging (OVA) for customers that cannot run Kubernetes.

Network diagram (textual)

- Customer VPC/Network: Subnet A (control plane agents), Subnet B (inference nodes), Subnet C (observability), Subnet D (model storage)
- Connectivity: Customer VPC <-> Redwood ControlPlane via AWS PrivateLink / Azure Private Endpoint / IPsec Tunnel.

Packaging and On-Prem Distribution

Purpose: enable reproducible customer installs with minimal manual steps and clear cryptographic provenance.

Packaging options

- Helm chart bundle (primary): contains manifests for operators, CRDs, webhooks, RBAC, and service objects. Versioned and signed with PGP/GPG.
- OCI image bundle: all required container images published to an internal registry; customers either pull from Redwood registry (private staging) or mirror to self-hosted registry during pre-install.
- Appliance bundle (OVA/VM): for air-gapped customers that accept a VM-based packaging.

Packaging requirements table

| Artifact | Format | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Control plane Helm chart | .tgz | Signed; includes CRDs and post-install validation jobs |
| Container images | OCI | Tagged by semver+build; digest pinned in values.yaml |
| Migration scripts | .sql / .sh | Idempotent, versioned, reversible |
| Packaging manifest | YAML | includes checksums and PGP signature reference |

Hardware and SW requirements (on-prem)

| Component | Minimum | Recommended |
|---|---:|---:|
| CPU (control plane nodes) | 4 vCPU | 8 vCPU |
| Memory (control plane) | 16 GB | 32 GB |
| GPU (inference) | n/a | 1 x A10 / H100 per replica depending on model |
| Disk | 200 GB SSD | 1 TB NVMe for model cache |
| Kubernetes | 1.24 | 1.26 |

Pre-install Checklist (Customer & Redwood)

1. Network: Confirm VPC peering/PrivateLink endpoints and required route tables.
2. DNS: Private DNS entries for control-plane endpoints provisioned.
3. IAM/Service accounts: RBAC roles and service principals provisioned.
4. Storage: S3-compatible bucket or NFS mount available and tested.
5. Observability: Prometheus scrape targets and Grafana endpoints accessible.
6. Backups: Snapshot policy and retention defined for critical KV stores.
7. Compliance: KMS/HSM integration confirmed for key management if required.

Installation Procedure (VPC Helm-based)

1. Mirror required images (if customer-mirrored): run mirror script and validate digests.
2. Install CRDs: kubectl apply -f crds.yaml --validate=false.
3. Install control plane Helm chart: helm upgrade --install redwood-control ./chart -f values-prod.yaml --namespace redwood-system --create-namespace --wait --timeout 15m.
4. Run post-install validation: ./scripts/post-install-validate.sh --namespace redwood-system.
5. Confirm health: kubectl get pods -n redwood-system (expect all pods Ready).

Post-install smoke tests

- API connectivity: curl -sS --cacert ca.pem https://control-plane.private.example.com/healthz -> 200
- Simple inference: run sample request against customer's ingress; verify 200 and expected response schema.
- Metric scrape: Prometheus target for control-plane present and scrape successful.

Day-2 Operations (Runbook highlights)

Monitoring and SLOs

- Baseline SLOs we recommend for private deployments:
  - Control plane API availability: 99.95% monthly
  - Inference tail latency (p50/p95 for 1k-token): p50 < 50ms, p95 < 250ms (hardware dependent)
  - Model load success rate: 99.9%

- Key metrics to export: pod_restarts, inference_latency_seconds (p50/p95/p99), model_load_time_seconds, kv_cache_hit_ratio, gpu_utilization_percent.

Logging and Tracing

- Structured JSON logs with request IDs (x-request-id) propagated across components.
- Correlate traces by request id; use Jaeger/Tempo for distributed tracing.

Scaling & Capacity

- Horizontal autoscaling recommended for worker nodes (HPA on queue length / GPU utilization).
- For predictable throughput use Dedicated pools configuration; document per-customer scaling policy.

Backups and Restore

- Daily snapshot of control-plane Postgres / etcd. Retain last 30 days.
- Model artifact versioning: maintain immutable S3 prefixes per model version.
- Restore test: quarterly restore to a staging namespace and run smoke tests.

Maintenance windows and change management

- Default maintenance window: weekly Tuesday 02:00-04:00 (customer local time).
- All changes follow change-management template: RFC -> canary rollout -> validation -> promote.

Upgrade & Rollback Procedures

Principles

- Upgrades are expressed as Helm releases with semantic versioning and migration scripts that are reversible where possible.
- Always run migrations in a canary/namespace before cluster-wide upgrade.

Pre-upgrade checklist

1. Confirm backups (DB, stateful sets, model store) are taken and validated.
2. Confirm that runbook and rollback steps are up-to-date for target version.
3. Verify health of existing cluster (no outstanding pod restarts, all Probes passing).

Canary rollout steps (control plane)

1. Create canary namespace: redwood-canary.
2. Deploy new control plane chart to redwood-canary and run validation suite.
3. If validations pass, perform a staggered upgrade: 10% of control-plane replicas -> 30% -> 100% with 30m observation windows.
4. Monitor key metrics and traces during each step.

Data plane (model-serving) upgrade notes

- Model-serving changes can impact hot KV cache and tokenization. Prefer gray-release model variants and compatibility shims.
- If model weights format changes, perform side-by-side rollout and route a subset of traffic to new variant.

Rollback procedure (fast path)

1. If canary fails or key SLOs degrade, mark new release as failed and scale earlier release to previous replica count: helm rollback redwood-control <previous_release>.
2. If DB migration is not reversible, run emergency restore from snapshot to an isolated staging namespace and fail traffic over to restored environment.
3. Post-rollback: open incident, triage cause, and produce RCA within 72 hours.

Runbook: Emergency rollback steps (short)

1. Notify stakeholders via PagerDuty and incident channel.
2. Scale down new control-plane deployment: kubectl scale deployment/redwood-control --replicas=0 -n redwood-system.
3. Helm rollback: helm rollback redwood-control <rev> -n redwood-system.
4. Validate health: kubectl get pods -n redwood-system; run smoke tests.

Customer Requirements Library (template entries)

- Networking: list of required CIDR ranges, egress policies, PrivateLink endpoints, expected latencies to Redwood control plane (<100ms recommended).
- Identity & Access: service principal provisioning steps, minimum RBAC policies, recommended role bindings.
- Storage: S3-compatible endpoint details, lifecycle policy, encryption at rest requirements (AES-256 or KMS).
- Security & Compliance: required audit logging retention (minimum 180 days), KMS/HSM integration, vulnerability scanning policy for container images.
- Observability: Prometheus scrape interval (15s), retention (30d hot, 365d cold), tracing sample rate (2-10%) and log retention.
- SLA & Support: target MTTR for Sev-1 incidents (2 hours for critical control-plane failures with Redwood-assist), support contact windows.

Acceptance test checklist (customer-run)

- Functional: inference request returns valid response for 95% of sample prompts.
- Performance: tail latency within agreed SLO by traffic class.
- Resilience: simulate node failure and validate automatic failover within 90s.

Common Troubleshooting Scenarios

- Model fails to load: check model bucket permissions, model artifact checksum, and controller logs (redwood-controller).
- High tail latency: analyze batching configuration, GPU utilization, and KV cache hit ratio.
- Control plane auth errors: validate service principal certificate expiry and KMS key policies.

Appendix: Useful CLI snippets

- Mirror images to customer registry:
  ./scripts/mirror-images.sh --source-registry=registry.redwood.ai --dest-registry=customer-registry.local --tag v2026.11.20

- Install Helm chart (example):
  helm upgrade --install redwood-control ./charts/redwood-control-1.4.0.tgz -f values/customer-values.yaml --namespace redwood-system --create-namespace --wait --timeout 20m

- Run post-install validation:
  ./scripts/post-install-validate.sh --namespace redwood-system --control-plane-endpoint https://control-plane.private.example.com
